name: Katherine Wiese (secretly Ecaterina, former Sabbat Bishop)

system.concept: Camarilla ancilla; secretly a centuries-old Brujah, former Sabbat bishop of New York

morality.path: Path of Power and the Inner Voice

system.biography:
Background

Eight centuries ago, a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} anarch named Ecaterina fled the Old World for New York, rose to become a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} bishop of the city, and grew disillusioned enough with the sect's degeneration to publicly denounce it at the Palla Grande — only to be struck down moments later by an @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} antitribu assassination team. She awoke nearly thirty years later in a disused subway electrical room, rescued by an unknown benefactor (in truth the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Yvette, who does not know Ecaterina's true identity), with no memory of who saved her and no way to know whether Archbishop Polonia himself ordered her death. Reinventing herself as Katherine Wiese, a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} ancilla of convenient luck, she now plays a careful, mercenary game in the reclaimed city's politics — determined to discover who she owes her survival to, resolve her suspicions about Polonia, and never again gamble her safety on any sect's cause.

Roleplaying Hints

Unlife is for surviving, not for grand causes. You weigh every situation for advantage and align with whoever is winning, though old pangs of guilt for abandoning the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}'s idealism still occasionally surface as rage or despair.
system.notes: Sire: Marhuel. True identity: Ecaterina, a former @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} bishop of New York believed destroyed in an @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} antitribu assassination attempt at the Palla Grande. Presence 6 in the book is capped to 5 for LARP play; other ratings above 5 have likewise been capped.

system.description:
Named for the legendary (and supposedly fae) progenitor of the houses of Anjou and Lusignan, this power lets a Toreador sway others through song. If the Artisan can phrase her request in the form of a song, her words take on the weight of a nigh-irresistible command.

System: The player states the suggestion she wishes to weave into the song and describes the song's nature. Everyone within earshot must resist or unknowingly submit to the request. The effect lasts as long as the Toreador continues singing or until the target leaves her presence; commands requiring the victim to leave the singer's presence can be resisted once more after the enchanting voice fades. Listeners outside the Toreador's immediate presence may notice something odd about the performance, though it registers as little more than an exceptionally fine one; other Toreador within earshot are immediately entranced. As a side benefit, knowledge of this power makes the character a superlative singer even when the power itself is not invoked.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)
system.duration: As long as the Toreador continues singing, or until the target leaves her presence

items.name: Presence — 3 Advanced — Pulse of the City

system.description: Your emotional state is always passively mirrored by the population of an entire city-sized region, with visitors affected less strongly than residents and vampires affected one level more mildly than mortals. To deliberately project a chosen emotion, spend a Willpower Trait and win a Static Social Challenge (typically 10-15 Traits, Storyteller's call) to shift the city's mood for one minute, extendable by spending additional Social Traits before the challenge. Two Methuselahs with this power contesting the same city test the Social Challenge directly against one another, with the longer-established Methuselah (six months or more) gaining five bonus Traits. Usable even while in torpor.
system.bloodCost: One Willpower Trait (plus Social Traits to extend duration)
system.duration: One minute per activation, longer with extra Social Traits spent

system.description:
A diplomat's most difficult task is understanding what people need to hear to make them agreeable to a suggestion. With this power, a Toreador learns what a target wants to hear. It does not reveal the target's full views, but it grants invaluable insight that can be put to use in negotiation, avoiding treachery, or worse — enemies may be allied, marriages arranged, and wars started with proper application of this knack.

System: The character concentrates on her subject and, on success, knows what to say to elicit a particular response. If she is attempting to advance an idea the target believes fundamentally wrong (convincing a pacifist monk to propose war, or a happy person to consider suicide), the target may resist. The effect lasts for the remainder of the conversation.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)

system.description: By spending a Blood Trait, you gain one additional action at the end of the turn, after all basic actions resolve.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By spending a Blood Trait, you preempt any physical action taken in the same turn that you are aware of, acting before your opponent can complete their move.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: You may make a single retest on any challenge of sheer physical strength, even against an opponent relying on stamina or speed to resist, at no cost.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Your unarmed and clubbing attacks inflict lethal rather than bashing damage if you choose. Once per game session you may also restore all of your used Brawny, Ferocious, Stalwart, Tough, and Wiry Physical Traits at once. Prowess costs nothing and isn't an action - it can be used at any time.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, p.150
